summary.title: Resources for Amateur Compiler Writers
summary.one_liner: A curated, opinionated reading list of compiler books and papers (parsing, SSA, register allocation, code generation, ABIs) chosen for practical amateur compiler writers.
takeaways: A set of recommended compiler textbooks, including the Dragon book for lexing/parsing and Muchnick for breadth of optimization topics
Key SSA papers: Cytron et al. for classic construction, Braun et al. for a lazy local construction method
Register allocation options: linear scan for fast JIT compilation vs. graph coloring (George & Appel; Smith, Ramsey & Holloway) for quality
Background references on ABIs (System V AMD64, ARM64 AAPCS), thread-local storage, and floating point
summary.summary: This is a personal annotated bibliography aimed at amateur compiler writers, listing books, papers, and reference documents the author found practical. Entries are grouped roughly by topic, including compiler textbooks, SSA form, dominance computation, constant propagation, register allocation, code generator generators, and platform ABIs. Each item has a short comment explaining why it is useful or its limitations. The page is a list rather than a tutorial, and the author notes the ordering is arbitrary and the selection is personal.
